messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @jamie_ops (on-call) — auth-service in us-west-2 reporting anomalous traffic: elevated 401s followed by spikes of S3 PUTs from a small set of service tokens. Investigate immediately.

jamie_ops: on it. I see the alert, pulling logs now. are we seeing token reuse or brute force?

maria_sre: copying logs to /tmp/triage. initial grep shows repeated Authorization: Bearer <svc-token> used across different EC2 instances — looks like a token copied into a build agent? snippet: ```2026-03-15T12:14:02Z auth-service ERROR token validation failed for token=svc-qt3A... src=10.12.8.45``` 

kevin_security: tagging potential compromise. Can you capture the full request headers (no bodies) and list the actor principals. Also isolate which S3 bucket received the PUTs.

jamie_ops: getting headers. S3 target: s3://redwood-logs-usw2-archive. PUTs look like small json files with stack traces. not huge, but suspicious — could be debug logs with tokens.

olivia_support: any customer-facing impact? have calls or log downloads happened?

maria_sre: quick check of access logs — only internal IP ranges and one external IP 52.86.23.101. Object ACLs look default private. No public read. So likely internal accidental exfil to our archive bucket rather than external leak. Still sensitive.

kevin_security: OK treat as credential exposure. Immediate actions: 1) Rotate affected service token, 2) Stop log shipper to that bucket, 3) Revoke any sessions using the token, 4) Block external IP at firewall. Who can rotate the token now?

jamie_ops: I can rotate. Which token id? maria, can you map token->service?

maria_sre: token svc-qt3A belongs to build-agent-usw2 (svc-account ci-runner). Creating rotation plan: generate new key, update config on runners, expire old key at 12:30 UTC. Will push a canary to one runner first.

incidents-bot: Incident #INC-2026-0315-77 created. Severity: P1 (credentials). Notifying Legal and Privacy.

kevin_security: I'll loop in Legal and send a short data-exposure assessment template. Olivia, please prepare a customer impact note in case any teams ask. Keep it internal for now.

olivia_support: drafting note: "We are investigating an incident affecting internal build logs that may contain service tokens. No evidence of external access; we are rotating affected tokens and will provide an update." Will post to #customers-ops after legal ok.

jamie_ops: rotation in progress. Command run: ```aws iam rotate-service-account-credentials --service-name ci-runner --region us-west-2 --output json``` applied to canary host now. Updating fleet via CI.

maria_sre: disabling log shipper: ```kubectl -n infra scale deploy log-forwarder --replicas=0``` — paused. Confirming no more PUTs to that bucket in the last 30s.

jamie_ops: firewall rule applied to block 52.86.23.101 at edge WAF and VPC NACL updated.

kevin_security: Legal/Privacy on the thread: @legal_team @privacy_team — files in bucket are internal debug logs. We have rotated tokens and stopped the shipper. Next: run quick discovery to find other buckets with similar ACLs and scan for tokens.

maria_sre: running grep for token patterns across S3 inventory (limited scope). ```aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-logs-usw2-archive --query 'Contents[].Key'``` then `s3 cp` each and grep. I'll upload results to /tmp/incident-2460123456.

incidents-bot: Pager duty note: Jamie acknowledged at 12:14 UTC. Mitigation steps underway.

olivia_support: Legal says hold customer comms until we confirm whether any tokens were actually present in the objects. If tokens found, we'll need to know which customers (if any) could be affected.

jamie_ops: found 3 objects with recognizable token patterns. Sample: ```{"timestamp":"2026-03-15T12:02:11Z","level":"debug","req":"Authorization: Bearer svc-qt3A..."}``` I'm saving full filenames to the incident folder.

kevin_security: escalate — assume secret exposure. Action items: (A) force rotate any credentials that could be derived, (B) search CI and runners for leaked token, (C) perform short-term revocation of sessions tied to svc-account, (D) communicate to privacy/legal. Who's owning (B)?

maria_sre: I'll own (B). Searching runner image layers and env vars across fleet. Running: ```ssh runner-canary 'grep -R "svc-qt3A" /var/lib/containers'```

jamie_ops: rotation done, old key disabled at 12:30 UTC. CI-runner rebooted and pulled new creds. Can confirm canary build passed. Scheduling rolling update now.

olivia_support: prepping internal incident summary for customers-ops, will wait for confirmation of scope.

maria_sre: grep across fleet returned one additional runner with token in /etc/ci/credentials — cleaning. Also found one archived image layer with the token string; initiating image rebuilds.

kevin_security: Good. We should also check log retention/forwarders to ensure PII isn't being forwarded externally. Any external connectors?

jamie_ops: no external S3 replication enabled on that bucket. Only internal archival. Confirmed.

incidents-bot: Update: mitigations applied. Severity downscoped to P2 for now pending inventory.

kevin_security: Next steps: complete inventory, rotate any other exposed creds, restore log shipper with filters to redact auth headers, file postmortem. Also prepare timeline for Legal. I will draft timeline; assign owners.

olivia_support: once Legal signs off, I'll coordinate a shared update to affected internal teams and prepare a short customer-facing message template.

jamie_ops: rolling update complete at 12:46 UTC. All runners have new creds. Logging shipper will remain disabled until redaction pipeline is in place.

maria_sre: scan results uploaded: /tmp/incident-2460123456/scan-results.txt — includes 4 objects with tokens and 2 runner configs. Starting redact+reingest plan.

kevin_security: thanks everyone. tagging in followups: postmortem owner @maria_sre, mitigation lead @jamie_ops, legal contact @kevin_security. Closing this thread when postmortem doc is created. :white_check_mark:
